No. The 2022 loss was not detected with Sentinel-2. It was mapped from Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13), which uses 30 m pixels and an annual series covering 2001–2025. Sentinel-2 isn't listed among the sources used. The JRC GFC2020 reference map (10 m) was used only to check forest status in 2020, and the MGAP 2021 map only gave context.

What the evidence shows:
- About 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022, or 3.41% of the 17.6 ha asset.
- The JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on all of the event area.
- Later years were observed, so the loss is corroborated under the method.
- Roughly 0.5 ha was in native forest and 0.1 ha outside mapped forest.

It does not establish whether deforestation occurred, the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.
